raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

FIX #60769

Fixes newline-separated parallel tool calls when using the generic Hermes parser with `tool_choice="required"`.

Hermes chat templates can produce a newline between consecutive tool calls:

```text
</tool_call>
<tool_call>
```

The `required` grammar currently expects an empty separator, so it can reject this otherwise valid output.

### Scope

This primarily affects models and configurations using the generic Hermes parser, including:
- NousResearch Hermes 2 Pro, Theta, and Hermes 3
- Models explicitly configured with `--tool-call-parser hermes`
- The Python frontend, where `qwen3_json` currently aliases the Hermes parser

Since #60136, the Rust frontend routes Qwen2.5, QwQ, and Qwen3 to its dedicated `qwen3_json` parser. Those automatically routed models are no longer the motivation for this change.

### Implementation

Override `build_call_format`, the extension point provided by the updated parser trait, so the Hermes `required` grammar accepts the newline used by the shipped template.

The change is scoped to the generic Hermes grammar. A separate Rust builder-side improvement or dedicated Python `qwen3_json` implementation would be complementary.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p vllm-parser
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked
```

Grammar checks on CPU: the template-rendered two- and three-call output of every Hermes-style template family above, plus the CI adapter's back-to-back framing, through the real `required` request path. End to end on 1x H200, greedy, `enable_thinking: false`, `--tool-call-parser hermes --enable-auto-tool-choice`: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B on the Python and Rust frontends and Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct on the Python frontend, main vs this PR, streaming and non-streaming.

## Test Result

Calls returned, 1x H200, greedy, `enable_thinking: false`; streaming and non-streaming identical in every cell:

| request | Qwen3-0.6B Rust, main | Qwen3-0.6B Rust, this PR | Qwen3-0.6B Python, main | Qwen3-0.6B Python, this PR | Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Python, main | Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Python, this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| required, one city | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| required, "Paris and Tokyo" | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 |
| required, three cities | 1 | 3 | 1 | 3 | 1 | 3 |
| required, weather in Rome + time in Sydney (two tools) | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 2 |
| named tool | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |
| auto, two cities | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| auto, three cities | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| required, two cities, `parallel_tool_calls=false` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 |

For the rows this PR should not change (one city, named, auto, `parallel_tool_calls=false`), the generated token IDs are identical to main in all three configurations.

- `pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_structural_tag_registry.py`: 263 passed. With main's `structural_tag_registry.py`, the 4 tests that encode the new behaviour fail. Removing the single-call limit (`limit_to_single_tool_call` call in `vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py`) fails 9 tests including the Hermes Chat and Responses ones; disabling it only for the Responses API fails the Responses test.
- `cargo test -p vllm-parser`: 621 passed; the new grammar snapshot test fails if the override returns the builder's format unchanged. Workspace `cargo nextest`: 2040 passed, 13 skipped. fmt and clippy clean.
- Templates: every family above is rejected by main's `required` grammar for two and three calls and accepted with this change; back-to-back calls are accepted by both; `parallel_tool_calls=false` accepts one call and rejects two with either separator.

Rebased onto main c723f6d3 on 2026-10-22, resolving a conflict with #62874 (`parse_into` now takes `DecodedText`); the override moved from `build_visible_format` to `build_call_format` following #60781. The H200 results above are from before the rebases; the Qwen3-0.6B Rust columns were measured with an explicit `--tool-call-parser hermes`.

AI assistance was used to investigate, write and test this change, and an independent automated review checked it.
